added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own baseline_suite and after_suite: logs/base-arm.log reports '221 passed' and logs/head-arm.log '223 passed', both at EXIT=0 with no failing id, so head-minus-base is empty over the same importer set; the head arm ran two more tests than the base because the node added two, and both arms ran to their summary line.

findings.text: follow-on: the payload emits moved_in and moved_off only inside the `if outcomes_at_requirement` block, under a comment stating the two are stated together because a move is counted at the request's requirement; the landed change makes both figures non-null and counts every move when the request names none, so that rationale is now false and the new no-requirement figures still never reach Jev — the branch the change added is exercised by the test but has no consumer-visible effect through prompts.py.

follow-on: the field comment reads "Both are null when the request names no requirement", which the landed change makes untrue; the annotation is now stale where the change it describes landed elsewhere.

follow-on: all four of the node's logs open with `# rev <sha> tree=...`, a shape reckon/crew/review.py:1331 _LOGGED_REVISION_RE does not parse (it requires the word `revision` on the first line), so annotate_review_of_run reads base_log_revision and head_log_revision as None for this run and the revision each arm measured is lost to every reader - verified by calling recorded_log_revision on logs/base-arm.log and logs/head-arm.log, both None, against a sibling run whose `revision: <sha> (base)` headers parse. The header also names 8ed7958f9 while the tree it measured carried the landed change at 983bff9f9. The added-failure count itself is unaffected (it reads the summary lines) and the review record carries the revision pair independently.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 8ed7958f9; 983bff9f9 makes moved_in/moved_off non-optional locals in _candidates_scan, replaces the two `is not None` guards with one shared requirement test, rewrites the docstring, makes both figures non-null in candidates(), adds the two tests and their header, and adds the evidence fragment; 127 insertions, 39 deletions, three files, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks for a two-moved-row test giving the receiving candidate moved_in of one and the chosen candidate moved_off of one, two and two when the request names no requirement, and a negative control that drops the filter and reads two; tests/test_a_move_counts_against_the_pick.py:302-373 adds exactly those two cases and logs/negative-control.log shows the dropped filter reddening the first of them at EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to count moved_in at the request's requirement as moved_off already was; reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:328-338 now gates the moved_in tally and the moved_off credit on the same test (`request_requirement is None or _recorded_requirement(row) == request_requirement`), and candidates() at :1196-1197 emits both non-null, so a moved row recorded at another requirement counts in neither figure.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the single commit, the three changed paths, the gate (7 passed, EXIT=0) with its log, the base and head arms (221 and 223 passed, 0 failures) with their logs, the negative control with its failing id and EXIT=1, the scratch base-arm module path and cwd, and one landing line, under status complete.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py, tests/test_a_move_counts_against_the_pick.py and docs/evidence/fragments/jev-learns-from-its-routes/moved-in-at-the-requirement.html; git show --stat 983bff9f9 lists those three and nothing else.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_move_counts_against_the_pick.py:302 asserts an exact gate dict and :373 asserts moved_off of 2, both against literals rather than a value the test handed in, and logs/negative-control.log shows reinstating the dropped filter reddens the first.
justifications.evidence: logs/gate-head.log reports "7 passed" at EXIT=0 and logs/negative-control.log reports "1 failed, 6 passed" at EXIT=1 with the id the head arm passes, but the reader cannot tie either to the commit it measured because all four logs name their revision in a shape reckon/crew/review.py:1331 does not parse.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:325-338 keeps the one-pass idiom and reuses _picked_backend_away and _recorded_requirement, and the added names carry no plan or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:334-337 counts a moved row in neither figure when its recorded requirement differs from the request's, which is the §15 deliverable.
justifications.reuse: the change extends the existing _candidates_scan rather than adding a mechanism, reusing _recorded_requirement at reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:244 for the filter that at_requirement already uses.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 983bff9f9 touches only reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py, tests/test_a_move_counts_against_the_pick.py and the evidence fragment, every one of them a declared write path.
